items.informal_name: Evaluation of Bivariate Polynomial at X Recovers Original Polynomial
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] {p : Polynomial (Polynomial R)},
  Polynomial.eval (Polynomial.C Polynomial.X)
      (Polynomial.eval₂ (Polynomial.mapRingHom (algebraMap R (Polynomial (Polynomial R)))) (Polynomial.C Polynomial.X)
        p) =
    p
items.informal_description: For any polynomial $ p $ in $ R[X][Y] $, evaluating $ p $ at $ Y = X $ (considered as a constant polynomial in $ R[X] $) results in $ p $ itself. This identity demonstrates that substituting the variable $ Y $ with the indeterminate $ X $ in the polynomial ring $ R[X][Y] $ preserves the original polynomial.

items.informal_name: Evaluation After Substitution Equals Evaluation at Substituted Value
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {σ : Type u_3} [inst : CommSemiring R] (f : σ → R) (i : σ) (p : Polynomial R),
  (MvPolynomial.eval f) ((Polynomial.toMvPolynomial i) p) = Polynomial.eval (f i) p
items.informal_description: For any function $ f : \sigma \to R $, any $ i \in \sigma $, and any polynomial $ p \in R[X] $, the evaluation of the multivariate polynomial obtained by substituting the variable $ X $ with $ X_i $ in $ p $, using $ f $, equals the evaluation of $ p $ at $ f(i) $. Formally, $ \text{eval}(f, p.\text{toMvPolynomial}(i)) = \text{eval}(f(i), p) $.

items.informal_name: Eval₂ Coincides with Ring Homomorphism on Multivariate Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {S : Type v} [inst : CommRing S] {R : Type u} (c : ℤ →+* S) (f : MvPolynomial R ℤ →+* S) (x : MvPolynomial R ℤ),
  MvPolynomial.eval₂ c (⇑f ∘ MvPolynomial.X) x = f x
items.informal_description: For any ring homomorphism $ f : R[\sigma] \to S $, coefficient map $ c : \mathbb{Z} \to S $, and polynomial $ x \in R[\sigma] $, evaluating $ x $ using the `eval₂` function with coefficient map $ c $ and variable map $ f \circ X $ yields the same result as applying $ f $ directly to $ x $, i.e., $ \text{eval}_2(c, f \circ X, x) = f(x) $.

items.informal_name: Evaluation Compatibility with Fin(n+1) to Fin(n) Equivalence
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {n : ℕ} {x : Fin n → R} [inst : CommSemiring R] (f : MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) R)
  (q : MvPolynomial (Fin n) R),
  (MvPolynomial.eval x) (Polynomial.eval q ((MvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv R n) f)) =
    (MvPolynomial.eval fun i => Fin.cases ((MvPolynomial.eval x) q) x i) f
items.informal_description: For any commutative semiring $ R $, natural number $ n $, evaluation map $ x : \text{Fin}(n) \to R $, multivariate polynomial $ f \in R[\text{Fin}(n+1)] $, and coefficient polynomial $ q \in R[\text{Fin}(n)] $, evaluating $ f $ after applying the $ \text{Fin}(n+1) $-to-\text{Fin}(n) algebra equivalence with outer variable substitution $ q $ is equivalent to directly evaluating $ f $ with the first variable replaced by $ q $ and other variables evaluated via $ x $. This establishes consistency between nested polynomial evaluations and direct evaluation under variable renaming.

items.informal_name: Evaluation Equivalence for Multivariate Polynomials over Fin(n+1) and Univariate Polynomials with Coefficients in Fin(n) Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} [inst : CommSemiring R] {n : ℕ} (s : Fin n → R) (y : R) (f : MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) R),
  (MvPolynomial.eval (Fin.cons y s)) f =
    Polynomial.eval y (Polynomial.map (MvPolynomial.eval s) ((MvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv R n) f))
items.informal_description: Evaluating a multivariate polynomial $ f $ in $ n+1 $ variables at a tuple $ (y, s_0, s_1, \ldots, s_n) $ is equivalent to first applying the $ \text{Fin}(n+1) \simeq \text{Option}(\text{Fin}(n)) $ variable equivalence to express $ f $ as a univariate polynomial in $ y $ with coefficients in $ n $-variable polynomials, then evaluating this outer polynomial at $ y $ after evaluating its coefficients using $ s $.

items.informal_name: Compatibility of Multivariate Polynomial Evaluation with Ring Homomorphism Composition
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {S₁ : Type v} {S₂ : Type w} {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : CommSemiring S₁]
  [inst_2 : CommSemiring S₂] (f : R →+* S₁) (g : σ → S₁) (φ : S₁ →+* S₂) (p : MvPolynomial σ R),
  φ ((MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom f g) p) = (MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom (φ.comp f) fun i => φ (g i)) p
items.informal_description: For any commutative semiring $R$, type $\sigma$, and ring homomorphisms $f : R \to S_1$, $g : \sigma \to S_1$, and $\phi : S_1 \to S_2$, the evaluation of a polynomial $p \in R[\sigma]$ satisfies $\phi(\mathrm{eval}_2(f, g, p)) = \mathrm{eval}_2(\phi \circ f, \phi \circ g, p)$. This expresses that applying $\phi$ after evaluation is equivalent to composing $\phi$ with the coefficient map and variable assignment before evaluation.

items.informal_name: Compatibility of Evaluation and Coefficient Mapping in Multivariate Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {S₁ : Type v} {S₂ : Type w} {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : CommSemiring S₁]
  [inst_2 : CommSemiring S₂] (f : R →+* S₁) (g : σ → S₂) (φ : S₁ →+* S₂) (p : MvPolynomial σ R),
  (MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom φ g) ((MvPolynomial.map f) p) = (MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom (φ.comp f) g) p
items.informal_description: For commutative semirings $R$, $S_1$, $S_2$, a type $\sigma$, ring homomorphism $f : R \to S_1$, variable assignment $g : \sigma \to S_2$, and ring homomorphism $\phi : S_1 \to S_2$, the evaluation of the polynomial $\mathrm{map}\,f\,p$ using $\phi$ and $g$ equals the evaluation of $p$ using the composed homomorphism $\phi \circ f$ and $g$. Formally, $\mathrm{eval}_2\,\phi\,g\, (\mathrm{map}\,f\,p) = \mathrm{eval}_2\, (\phi \circ f)\,g\,p$ for all $p \in R[\sigma]$.

items.informal_name: Compatibility of Multivariate Polynomial Evaluation with Coefficient Mapping
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {S₁ : Type v} {S₂ : Type w} {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : CommSemiring S₁]
  [inst_2 : CommSemiring S₂] (f : R →+* S₁) (g : σ → S₂) (φ : S₁ →+* S₂) (p : MvPolynomial σ R),
  MvPolynomial.eval₂ φ g ((MvPolynomial.map f) p) = MvPolynomial.eval₂ (φ.comp f) g p
items.informal_description: For any commutative semiring $R$, type $\sigma$, and commutative semirings $S_1, S_2$, given a ring homomorphism $f : R \to S_1$, a variable assignment $g : \sigma \to S_2$, and a ring homomorphism $\phi : S_1 \to S_2$, the evaluation of the polynomial $\mathrm{map}\, f\, p$ using coefficient map $\phi$ and variable map $g$ equals the evaluation of $p$ using the composed coefficient map $\phi \circ f$ and variable map $g$. Formally, $\mathrm{eval}_2(\phi, g, \mathrm{map}\, f\, p) = \mathrm{eval}_2(\phi \circ f, g, p)$ for all $p \in R[\sigma]$.

items.informal_name: Compatibility of Multivariate Polynomial Evaluation with Composed Ring Homomorphisms
items.informal_description: For any commutative semiring $S_2$, ring homomorphism $k : S_1 \to S_2$, ring homomorphism $f : R \to S_1$, variable assignment $g : \sigma \to S_1$, and polynomial $p$, applying $k$ to the evaluation of $p$ using $f$ on coefficients and $g$ on variables equals evaluating the polynomial $\mathrm{map}\,f\,p$ using $k \circ g$ on variables and $k$ on coefficients. Formally: $k(\mathrm{eval}_2\,f\,g\,p) = \mathrm{eval}_2\,k\,(k \circ g)\,(\mathrm{map}\,f\,p)$.

items.informal_name: Evaluation of Multivariate Polynomials Composes with Ring Homomorphisms
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {S₁ : Type v} {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : CommSemiring S₁] (f : R →+* S₁)
  (g : σ → R) (p : MvPolynomial σ R), f ((MvPolynomial.eval g) p) = MvPolynomial.eval₂ f (⇑f ∘ g) p
items.informal_description: For any ring homomorphism $ f : R \to S_1 $, any map $ g : \sigma \to R $, and any polynomial $ p \in R[\sigma] $, it holds that $ f(\mathrm{eval}_g(p)) = \mathrm{eval}_{f, f \circ g}(p) $, where $ \mathrm{eval}_g $ denotes evaluation using variable map $ g $ and identity coefficient map, and $ \mathrm{eval}_{f, f \circ g} $ denotes evaluation using coefficient map $ f $ and variable map $ f \circ g $.

items.informal_name: Compatibility of Composition with Algebra Evaluation Homomorphism
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {S₁ : Type v} {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : CommSemiring S₁] [inst_2 : Algebra R S₁]
  (f : σ → S₁) {B : Type u_2} [inst_3 : CommSemiring B] [inst_4 : Algebra R B] (φ : S₁ →ₐ[R] B),
  φ.comp (MvPolynomial.aeval f) = MvPolynomial.aeval fun i => φ (f i)
items.informal_description: For any commutative semiring $B$ equipped with an $R$-algebra structure and any algebra homomorphism $\phi : S_1 \to B$ over $R$, the composition of $\phi$ with the multivariate polynomial evaluation homomorphism $\text{aeval}_f$ equals the evaluation homomorphism $\text{aeval}_{\phi \circ f}$, where $f : \sigma \to S_1$ is a variable assignment. This expresses that applying $\phi$ after polynomial evaluation is equivalent to first composing $\phi$ with the variable assignment and then evaluating.

items.informal_name: Compatibility of Composition with Multivariate Polynomial Evaluation
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {S₁ : Type v} {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : CommSemiring S₁] [inst_2 : Algebra R S₁]
  (f : σ → S₁) {B : Type u_2} [inst_3 : CommSemiring B] [inst_4 : Algebra R B] (φ : S₁ →ₐ[R] B) (p : MvPolynomial σ R),
  φ ((MvPolynomial.aeval f) p) = (MvPolynomial.aeval fun i => φ (f i)) p
items.informal_description: For any $ R $-algebra homomorphism $ \varphi : S_1 \to B $ and polynomial $ p \in R[\sigma] $, applying $ \varphi $ to the evaluation of $ p $ at a variable assignment $ f : \sigma \to S_1 $ equals the evaluation of $ p $ at the composed assignment $ \varphi \circ f $, i.e., $ \varphi(\text{aeval}_f(p)) = \text{aeval}_{\varphi \circ f}(p) $.

items.informal_name: Composition of Algebra Map and Evaluation Equals Original Homomorphism
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] {S : Type u_2} {A : Type u_3} [inst_1 : CommSemiring S]
  [inst_2 : CommSemiring A] [inst_3 : Algebra S R] [inst_4 : Algebra S A] (g : R →ₐ[S] A) (y : σ → A),
  (↑(MvPolynomial.aevalTower g y)).comp (algebraMap R (MvPolynomial σ R)) = ↑g
items.informal_description: The composition of the evaluation homomorphism $\text{aevalTower}_g(y)$ with the canonical algebra map from $R$ to the multivariate polynomial ring $R[\sigma]$ equals the original ring homomorphism $g$ from $R$ to $A$. This means that evaluating a polynomial whose coefficients are embedded via the algebra structure recovers the original homomorphism $g$.

items.informal_name: Compatibility of Multivariate Polynomial Evaluation with Ring Homomorphisms
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {S₁ : Type v} {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : CommSemiring S₁] [inst_2 : Algebra R S₁]
  {B : Type u_2} [inst_3 : CommSemiring B] (g : σ → S₁) (φ : S₁ →+* B) (p : MvPolynomial σ R),
  φ ((MvPolynomial.aeval g) p) = (MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom (φ.comp (algebraMap R S₁)) fun i => φ (g i)) p
items.informal_description: For any commutative semiring $ R $, type $ \sigma $, commutative semiring $ S_1 $ with an $ R $-algebra structure, and commutative semiring $ B $, given a variable assignment $ g : \sigma \to S_1 $, a ring homomorphism $ \varphi : S_1 \to B $, and a polynomial $ p \in R[\sigma] $, applying $ \varphi $ to the algebra evaluation $ \mathrm{aeval}_g(p) $ equals evaluating $ p $ using the composed ring homomorphism $ \varphi \circ \mathrm{algebraMap}_{R \to S_1} $ on coefficients and $ \varphi \circ g $ on variables. Symbolically, $ \varphi(\mathrm{aeval}_g(p)) = \mathrm{eval}_2^{\varphi \circ \mathrm{algebraMap}, \varphi \circ g}(p) $.

items.informal_name: Compatibility of Multivariate Evaluation with Univariate Embedding
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {S : Type u_2} {σ : Type u_3} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : CommSemiring S] [inst_2 : Algebra R S]
  (f : σ → S) (i : σ), (MvPolynomial.aeval f).comp (Polynomial.toMvPolynomial i) = Polynomial.aeval (f i)
items.informal_description: For any function $ f : \sigma \to S $ and any index $ i \in \sigma $, the composition of the multivariate polynomial evaluation homomorphism $ \operatorname{aeval}_f $ with the univariate embedding $ \operatorname{toMvPolynomial}_i $ is equal to the univariate polynomial evaluation homomorphism at $ f(i) $. Formally, $ \operatorname{aeval}_f \circ \operatorname{toMvPolynomial}_i = \operatorname{aeval}(f(i)) $.
